2.reason: Steady (constant) speed means zero acceleration, so by Newton's first law the net force is zero - the forces are balanced.

3.reason: Force = rate of change of momentum = (dm/dt) x v = 1 kg/s x 60000 m/s = 60000 N. (60 km/s = 60000 m/s.)

5.reason: Action (sailor pushed forward) and reaction (boat pushed backward) are equal and opposite - Newton's third law of motion.

8.reason: The gun exerts a forward force on the bullet (action); by Newton's third law the gun recoils backward onto the arm. Among the options the correct action is a forward force on the bullet.

9.reason: Friction is the force that always opposes the relative motion of one body over another.

14.reason: Inertia -> Mass of the object (B); Friction -> Necessary evil (D); Momentum -> Product of mass and velocity (A); Force -> Rate of change of momentum (C). So 1-B, 2-D, 3-A, 4-C.

15.reason: First law -> rest/uniform motion unless force (B); Second law -> acceleration proportional to force (A); Third law -> equal and opposite reaction (C); Galileo's law of inertia -> object at rest/uniform motion unless unbalanced force (D). So 1-B, 2-A, 3-C, 4-D.

16.reason: F = m x a (d); P (momentum) = m x v (a); dP relates to (P2-P1)/t (c); momentum before collision = momentum after collision are equal (b). So (i)-d, (ii)-a, (iii)-c, (iv)-b.

17.reason: Friction -> opposes motion (C); Limiting friction -> force just sufficient to move (B); Sliding friction -> sufficient to slide one over another (D); Rolling friction -> when one rolls over another (A). So 1-C, 2-B, 3-D, 4-A.

18.reason: Force -> Newton (A); Momentum -> Kg m/s (C); Unbalanced force -> Acceleration (B); Principle on which rocket works -> Newton's third law (D). So 1-A, 2-C, 3-B, 4-D.

19.reason: Action and reaction -> act on different objects (C); Magnitude of force -> Newton's second law (B); Momentum -> vector quantity (D); Resultant of balanced force -> no acceleration (A). So 1-C, 2-B, 3-D, 4-A.

20.reason: Inertia -> the tendency to do nothing (iv); Friction -> necessary evil (i); Momentum -> product of mass and velocity (iii); Force -> rate of change of momentum (ii). So (a)-iv, (b)-i, (c)-iii, (d)-ii.

21.reason: Cause of acceleration -> Force (iv); quantitative measure of inertia -> Mass (i); powder on carrom board -> decreases friction (iii); rough tyres -> increases friction (ii). So (a)-iv, (b)-i, (c)-iii, (d)-ii.

22.reason: Cart pulled by horse, backward push (walking) and worn-out shoe recoil all illustrate Newton's 3rd law (iii); recoiling of gun is the standard example of conservation of momentum (i). Option C maps three to (iii) and gun to (i). REVIEW: 'recoil of shoe worn out' is loosely worded; option C is the only choice assigning three (iii) and one (i).

23.reason: Cause of acceleration -> Force (D); quantitative measure of inertia -> Mass (A); powder on carrom board -> decreases friction (C); rough tyres -> increases friction (B). So 1-D, 2-A, 3-C, 4-B.

24.reason: Cart pulled by horse -> Newton's III law (B); backward push (walking) -> Newton's III law (B); sole of shoe worn out -> friction (A); recoiling of gun -> conservation of momentum (C). So 1-B, 2-B, 3-A, 4-C.

25.reason: Unbalanced force -> Force (iii); remains unchanged -> inertia (iv); method of reducing friction -> applying grease (i); rate of change of momentum -> change in state (ii). REVIEW: 'rate of change of momentum' is really Force, but Force(iii) is used for (a); option A is the only internally-consistent one-to-one mapping offered.

26.reason: Unbalanced force -> Force (C); unchanging tendency -> ... option A reads 1-C, 2-B, 3-D, 4-A. REVIEW: mapping is ambiguous; option A assigns Force(C) to unbalanced force and grease(A) to rate of change, the only internally-consistent printed key.

27.reason: Friction -> force which opposes motion (iv); Limiting friction -> just sufficient to move (i); Sliding friction -> slide one over another (iii); Rolling friction -> rolls over another (ii). Ideal is (a)-iv,(b)-i,(c)-iii,(d)-ii, not offered exactly. REVIEW: option D (a)-iv,(b)-i,(c)-ii,(d)-iii is the closest printed key (friction->opposes and limiting->just-sufficient correct).

28.reason: With no external force, total momentum is conserved (law of conservation of momentum).

29.reason: Running first gives him inertia of motion, which helps carry him forward into a long jump.

30.reason: Forces always occur in action-reaction pairs, so an isolated (single) force cannot exist. The printed wording 'isolated' best captures this. REVIEW: 'single' (A) is an equally valid phrasing; choosing 'isolated' (B) as the more textbook term.

31.reason: Newton's second law: rate of change of momentum is directly proportional to the applied force.

32.reason: Balanced forces cause no acceleration and cannot move or retard a body, but can change its shape - deform it.

33.reason: When a branch is shaken the branch moves but the leaves tend to stay at rest due to inertia, so they detach - inertia.

34.reason: Inertia is of three types: inertia of rest, inertia of motion, and inertia of direction.

35.reason: Newton's first law gives the qualitative definition of force (it tells what force does, not how much).

36.reason: Momentum is the total quantity of motion contained in a moving body. Among the options, 'motion' fits.

37.reason: The gun recoils to conserve total momentum (zero before firing, so the bullet's forward momentum is balanced by the gun's backward recoil).

38.reason: Gravitational force is the weakest fundamental force (A true). Electrostatic force acts without contact - a non-contact force (B true). Both true.

39.reason: Rockets carry their own oxidiser since there is no air in space (A true). Jet planes take oxygen from the atmosphere (B true). Both true.

40.reason: When a bus suddenly STARTS forward, the passenger falls BACKWARD (inertia of rest), not forward - so A is false. A gun recoils backward at a smaller speed than the bullet - B is true. So only B is true.

41.reason: A spring force can push (compressed) OR pull (stretched), so statement 1 is incorrect. Statement 1 corresponds to (A) = option D.

42.reason: Action and reaction ARE equal (so '1. They are not equal' is incorrect) and act on DIFFERENT objects (so '3. They are on same object' is incorrect). Incorrect statements are 1 and 3 = A and C.

43.reason: Accelerated motion: velocity changes (1/A), speed changes (2/B), a force acts (3/C); mass does not change (4/D false). So A, B and C are correct.

44.reason: Action-reaction ARE equal (1 incorrect) and act on DIFFERENT objects (3 incorrect). Incorrect statements are 1 and 3 = A and C.

45.reason: 1 (A) correct (friction retards, gravity can retard or accelerate). 3 (C) correct (friction needs contact). 4 (D) correct (gravity acts at height). 2 (B) false (gravity can accelerate). So A, C and D = option C.

46.reason: Action-reaction pairs do NOT require contact (e.g. gravitational/electrostatic action-reaction acts at a distance), so 'they act only between bodies in contact' is the incorrect statement.

47.reason: 1 (A) correct, 3 (C) correct, 4 (D) correct; 2 (B) false ('both produce retardation'). So A, C and D = option B.

48.reason: Accelerated straight motion: velocity changes (A), speed changes (B), force acts (C); mass does not change (D false). So A, B and C = option B.

49.reason: Action and reaction are equal (A), act simultaneously (C) and are opposite in direction (D), but act on DIFFERENT bodies - so 'act on the same bodies' (B) is incorrect.
